<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Non-interest income totaled $14.3 million in 2013, an increase of $1.3 million or 10.0% over $13.0 million in 2012.&#160; Non-interest income of $13.0 million in 2012 represented an increase of $3.1 million or 30.8% over $9.9 million in 2011.&#160; Non-interest income generally consists primarily of service charge income on deposit accounts, international fee income, gains recognized on sales of SBA loans, warrant income and gains on sales of other real estate owned (OREO) and securities.&#160; The increase in non-interest income during the year ending December&nbsp;31, 2013 was primarily attributable to an increase in gains on sales of SBA loans, gains on sale of securities and service charges on deposit accounts, partially offset by decreases in gains from the sale of OREO.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The increase in non-interest income during the year ending December&nbsp;31, 2012 was primarily attributable to an increase in warrant income. Additionally, non-interest income benefitted during 2012 by increased gains on sale of OREO and service charges on deposit accounts.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 service charge income on deposit accounts was $3.7 million, representing an increase of $320,000, or 9.5%, compared to $3.4 million for the same period one year ago.&#160; The service charge income on deposit accounts for 2012 compared to $2.9 million in 2011, representing an increase of $478,000 or 16.6%. The increase in 2013 and 2012 was attributable to an increase in the deposit portfolio and deposit related analysis charges.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company generates international fee income on spot contracts (binding agreements for the purchase or sale of currency for immediate delivery and settlement) and forward contracts (a contractual commitment for a fixed amount of foreign currency on a future date at an agreed upon exchange rate) in connection with client&#146;s cross-border activities. The transactions incurred are during the ordinary course of business and are not speculative in nature.&#160; The Company recognizes income on a cash basis at the time of contract settlement in an amount equal to the spread created by the exchange rate charged to the client versus the actual exchange rate negotiated by the Company in the open market.&#160; During 2013, the Company recognized $2.7 million in international fee income, representing an increase of $57,000, or 2.2%, compared to $2.6 million for the same period one year ago.&#160; During 2012, the Company recognized $2.6 million in international fee income, representing an increase of $158,000, or 6.4%, compared to $2.5 million in 2011.&#160; The increase in international fee income in both 2013 and 2012 was primarily caused by an increase in client demand for international services.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">26<a name="PB_26_174426_5796"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue from sales of SBA loans is dependent on consistent origination and funding of new loan volumes, the timing of which may be impacted, from time to time, by (1)&nbsp;increased competition from other lenders; (2)&nbsp;the relative attractiveness of SBA borrowing to other financing options; (3)&nbsp;adjustments to programs by the SBA; (4)&nbsp;changes in activities of secondary market participants and; (5)&nbsp;other factors.&#160;&#160; During 2013, the Company recognized $2.7 million in gains on sale of SBA loans, representing an increase of $832,000 or 45.0% over the prior year.&#160; The Company recognized $1.9 million in gains on sales of SBA loans in 2012 compared to $1.7 million in 2011, representing an increase of $107,000 or 6.1%. The increase in gains on sale of SBA loans is a direct result of an increase in SBA loans sold in the current period versus the same period last year.&#160; During 2013, the Company&#146;s SBA group funded $65.0 million in new loans and sold $46.3 million, which included $13.5 million in loans funded in the previous year.&#160; This compares to $54.5 million funded and $37.3 million sold in the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, which included $12.0 million in loans funded in the previous year. For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, the Company&#146;s SBA group funded $35.5 million in new loans and sold $26.6 million, which included $13.9 million in loans funded in the previous year.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Income from warrants is inherently event-driven and the contributions from warrants largely reflect the economic environment of IPOs and M&amp;A activity. During 2013, the Company recognized $1.3 million in warrant income. This represented a decrease of $161,000 or 11.3% from $1.4 million in 2012. During the first nine months of 2012, the Company redeemed several warrants. In 2012, warrant income increased $1.0 million or 262.8%, compared to $392,000 in 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company recognized gains on the sale of securities of $804,000 during the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 which represents an increase of $481,000 or 148.9% compared to $323,000 during 2012.&#160; During 2011 the Company recognized $438,000 in gain on the sale of securities. Compared to 2011, the decrease in gains on the sale of securities in 2012 represented $115,000 or 26.3%.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company earns a servicing fee on all SBA loans sold.&#160; During 2013, $488,000 in SBA loan servicing income was recognized compared to $514,000 for the prior year, reflecting a decrease of $26,000 or 5.1%. The $514,000 recognized in 2012 represents an increase of $103,000 or 25.1% over $411,000 in 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2013, 2012, and 2011, the Company recognized $470,000, $1.1 million, and $421,000, respectively, in gains on the sale of OREO properties. For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, the lower level of gains was&#160; reflective of decreased balances of OREO as a result of the Company&#146;s successful resolution efforts.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company fully implemented a Visa card program during the current year, which contributed $914,000 in non-interest income in 2013, and a modest $112,000 in non-interest income during 2012.&#160; There was no income recognized as a result of this program in 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net interest income and non-interest income comprised total revenue of $82.6 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, compared to $73.6 million for the same period one year earlier, and $58.4 million in 2011.&#160; This represented an increase of $9.0 million, or 12.2% in 2013, and an increase of $15.2 million, or 26.1% in 2012.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Non-interest expenses were $51.9 million in 2013 as compared to $46.2 million in 2012 and $42.4 million in 2011.&#160; Non-interest expense increased approximately $3.2 million in 2013 compared to 2012.&#160; This increase was generally widespread across all categories. As a percentage of average earning assets, other expenses were 3.6%, 3.8%, and 4.1% for the years 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.&#160; Overall, trends in non-interest expenses in 2013 reflect a higher level of expense related to supporting growth and investments in new initiatives.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Non-interest expense increased approximately $3.8 million in 2012 compared to 2011.&#160; This increase was primarily attributable to increased salaries and benefits, marketing costs and data processing expense. Overall, trends in non-interest expenses in 2012 reflect a lower level of expense related to problem asset valuation and resolution and higher expenses related to supporting growth and investments in new initiatives.&#160; Non-interest expenses measured as a percentage of average assets were 3.6% in 2013, 3.8% in 2012 and 4.1% in 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Salaries and related benefits was the largest component of the Bank&#146;s non-interest expense.&#160; Salaries and benefits were $33.5 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 as compared to $30.3 million and $24.6 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 and 2011, respectively.&#160; The Bank had 235 full time equivalent employees (FTE) at December&nbsp;31, 2013 as compared to 207 FTE at December&nbsp;31, 2012 and 193 FTE at December&nbsp;31, 2011.&#160; The increase in salaries and related benefits in 2013 compared to 2012 and 2011 was primarily attributable to the increase in headcount to support growth and new initiatives combined with annual salary increases necessary to remain competitive in the Company&#146;s core markets and increased stock-based compensation due to long term retention awards.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Occupancy expense for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 was $4.1 million, compared to $4.0 million during 2012, which represents an increase of $110,000 or 2.8%.&#160; Occupancy expense for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 represented an increase of approximately $192,000, or 5.1% over $3.8 million in 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company contracts with third-party vendors for most data processing needs and to support technical infrastructure.&#160; Data processing expense in 2013 was $3.8 million which represented an increase of approximately $518,000 over $3.3 million one year earlier.&#160; Data processing expense in 2012 represented an increase of approximately $211,000 over $3.0 million one year earlier.&#160; The increase in data processing in both years was primarily due to an increase in deposit transaction volumes.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Legal and professional expenses were $1.7 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, which represents a $520,000 increase compared to $1.2 million one year earlier.&#160;&#160; Legal and professional expenses were $2.7 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011.&#160; The increase in legal fees in 2013 was primarily a result of an increase of non-performing loans. The increase in legal and professional expenses in 2012 was primarily due to the early redemption of Series&nbsp;C preferred shares and repurchase of the related warrant, as well as legal fees associated with the active management of one non-real estate credit exposure.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory assessments related to FDIC insurance pertaining to deposit balances, totaled $1.2 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, compared to $879,000 for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 and $1.7 million in 2011.&#160; Regulatory assessments fluctuate depending on asset size and other factors, including credit quality.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">OREO and loan related charges were $1.0 million in 2013, compared to $995,000 in 2012, representing an increase of $51,000 or 5.1%. The increase in OREO and loan related charges was primarily attributed to an increase in nonperforming loans.&#160; OREO and loan related charges decreased $775,000 or 43.8% in 2012 from $1.8 million in 2011.&#160; The decrease in OREO and loan related charges during 2012 was primarily attributed to a decrease in nonperforming assets in 2012 compared to 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s efficiency ratio, the ratio of non-interest expenses to revenues, was 62.76% for the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, compared to 62.81% and 72.68% for the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 and December&nbsp;31, 2011, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Income Taxes</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s effective tax rate was 40.3% for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, 41.0% for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 and 41.2% for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011.&#160; See Note 8 to the consolidated financial statements for additional information on income taxes.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

The results of operations are not necessarily indicative of results for any future period. The following table shows the Company&#146;s unaudited quarterly income statement data for the years 2013 and 2012.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Financial Condition and Earning Assets</font></u></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2013, total assets were $1.6 billion, gross loans were $1.1 billion and deposits were $1.4 billion. Assets increased $260.5 million, or 19.4%, from $1.3 billion at December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; Gross loans increased $169.1 million, or 18.6%, from $908.6 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; Deposits increased $243.5 million, or 20.9%, from $1.2 billion at December&nbsp;31, 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2012, total assets were $1.3 billion, gross loans were $908.6 million and deposits were $1.2 billion. Assets increased $182.6 million, or 15.7%, from $1.2 billion at December&nbsp;31, 2011.&#160; Gross loans increased $146.6 million, or 19.2%, from $762.0 million at December&nbsp;31, 2011.&#160; Deposits increased $163.9 million, or 16.4%, from $998.7 million at December&nbsp;31, 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Federal Funds Sold</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Federal funds sold were $162.4 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013 as compared to $113.8 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; The Company&#146;s investment in federal funds sold reflects the Company&#146;s current strategy of deploying other earning assets primarily in federal funds sold to address the potential volatility of deposit balances and to accommodate projected loan growth.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The average balance of federal funds sold was $122.0 million in 2013 and $86.7 million in 2012.&#160; These balances represented 9.8% and 8.5% of average deposits for 2013 and 2012, respectively.&#160; They are maintained primarily for the short-term liquidity needs of the Bank.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Securities</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Investment securities are classified as available for sale, held to maturity or trading securities.&#160; Any unrealized gain or loss on investment securities available for sale is reflected in the carrying value of the security and reported net of income taxes in the equity section of the balance sheet.&#160; Held-to maturity securities are recorded at amortized cost, adjusted for the amortization or accretion of premiums or discounts. Any unrealized gain or loss on trading securities is recorded in the income statement. The pre-tax unrealized loss on securities available for sale at December&nbsp;31, 2013 was $1.9 million, while the pre-tax unrealized gain on securities available for sale at December&nbsp;31, 2012 was $2.9 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Loan Portfolio</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table shows the Company&#146;s loans by type and their percentage distribution at December&nbsp;31, 2013, 2012, 2011, 2010, and 2009.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%" style="border-collapse:collapse;width:100.0%;">

<td width="1%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0.375pt 0in;width:1.0%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">%</font></p>    </td>   </tr>

<td width="2%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:2.5%;">

<td width="1%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 2.25pt 0in;width:1.0%;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gross loan balances increased to $1.1 billion at December&nbsp;31, 2013, which represented an increase of $169.1 million or 18.6% as compared to $908.6 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012. The increase in total gross loans was broad-based throughout the portfolio, with the most significant growth reflected in the commercial, SBA lending, and construction portfolios, and was a result of a concerted effort to prudently grow the balance of loans in our portfolio while managing risk.&#160; Gross loan balances of $908.6 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012, represented an increase of $146.6 million or 19.2% as compared to $762.0 million at December&nbsp;31, 2011. The increase in loans was primarily attributable to growth in the commercial and factoring/asset based lending portfolio.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s commercial loan portfolio represents loans to small and middle-market businesses primarily in the Santa Clara county region as well as loans to technology-based emerging growth companies.&#160; Commercial loans were $585.6 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013, which represented an increase of $149.3 million or 34.2% over $436.3 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2013, commercial loans comprised 54.3% of total loans outstanding as compared to 48.0% at December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160;&#160; Commercial loans were $436.3 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012, which represented an increase of $105.9 million or 32.1% versus $330.3 million at December&nbsp;31, 2011.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2012, commercial loans comprised 48.0% of total loans outstanding as compared to 43.4% at December&nbsp;31, 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Approximately 47% of the Company&#146;s construction loan portfolio consists of loans to finance individual single-family residential homes in markets in the Peninsula and South Bay region of Silicon Valley.&#160; The remainder is comprised of commercial and multi-family development projects.&#160; Construction loans increased $16.0 million, or 45.1%, to $51.5 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013 as compared to $35.5 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; Construction loan balances at December&nbsp;31, 2013 comprised 4.8% of total loans compared to 3.9% at December&nbsp;31, 2012. Construction loans decreased $11.7 million, or 24.8%, to $35.5 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012 as compared to $47.2 million at December&nbsp;31, 2011.&#160; Construction loan balances at December&nbsp;31, 2012 and 2011 comprised 3.9% and 6.2% of total loans, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s land loan portfolio consists of land and land development loans related to future construction credits.&#160; Land loans increased $4.6 million or 51.3% to $13.6 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013 as compared to $9.0 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; Land loan balances at December&nbsp;31, 2013 comprised 1.3% of total loans as compared to 1.0% at December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; Land loans increased $2.2 million to $9.0 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012 compared to $6.8 million at December&nbsp;31, 2011.&#160; Land loan balances at December&nbsp;31, 2012 comprised 1.0% of total loans as compared to 0.9% at December&nbsp;31, 2011.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">32<a name="PB_32_171511_7748"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other real estate loans consist of commercial real estate and home equity lines of credit.&#160; Other real estate loans decreased $17.9 million, or 12.8%, to $122.1 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013 as compared to $139.9 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to other real estate term loans. The decrease in other real estate loans was primarily in owner occupied real estate term loans.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2013, other real estate term loans were primarily comprised of office and industrial investment properties which represented approximately 41% of the total and approximately 42% were to finance buildings occupied by clients of the bank.&#160; Approximately 15% of term real estate loans at December&nbsp;31, 2013 were to finance retail properties.&#160; Other real estate loans decreased $17.5 million or 11.1% to $139.9 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012 as compared to $157.4 million at December&nbsp;31, 2011.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to other real estate term loans. The decrease in other real estate loans was primarily in owner occupied real estate term loans. At December&nbsp;31, 2012, other real estate term loans were primarily comprised of office and industrial investment properties which represented approximately 44% of the total and approximately 42% were to finance buildings occupied by clients of the bank.&#160; Approximately 17% of term real estate loans at December&nbsp;31, 2012 were to finance retail properties.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Factoring and asset-based lending represents purchased accounts receivable (factoring) and a structured accounts receivable lending program where the Company receives client specific payment for client invoices.&#160; Under the factoring program, the Company purchases accounts receivable invoices from its clients and then receives payment directly from the party obligated for the receivable.&#160;&#160; In most cases the Company purchases the receivables subject to recourse from the Company&#146;s factoring client.&#160; The asset-based lending program requires a security interest in all of a client&#146;s accounts receivable.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2013, factoring and asset based loans totaled $192.8 million or 17.9% of total loans as compared to $195.3 million or 21.5% of total loans at December&nbsp;31, 2012. This compares to $142.5 million or 18.7% of total loans at December&nbsp;31, 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The SBA line of business operates primarily in Santa Clara County. The Company, as a Preferred Lender, originates SBA loans and participates in the SBA 7A and 504 SBA lending programs.&#160; Under the 7A program, a loan is made for commercial or real estate purposes.&#160; The SBA guarantees these loans and the guarantee may range from 75% to 90% of the total loan. In addition, the loan could be collateralized by a deed of trust on real estate.&#160; Under the 504 program, the Company lends directly to the borrower and takes a first deed of trust to the subject property.&#160; In addition the SBA, through a Certified Development Corporation, makes an additional loan to the borrower and takes a deed of trust subject to the Company&#146;s position. At December&nbsp;31, 2013, SBA loans comprised $106.4 million, or 9.9%, of total loans, an increase of $19.0 million, or 21.8%, from $87.4 million or 9.6% of total loans at December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; SBA loans increased by $14.0 million or 19.14% in 2012 from $73.3 million or 9.6% in total loans at December&nbsp;31,2011.&#160;&#160; The Company has the ability and the intent to sell all or a portion of the SBA loans and, as such, carries the saleable portion of SBA loans at the lower of aggregate cost or fair value.&#160;&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2013, 2012 and 2011 the fair value of SBA loans exceeded aggregate cost and therefore, SBA loans were carried at aggregate cost.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other loans consist primarily of loans to individuals for personal uses, such as installment purchases, overdraft protection loans and a variety of other consumer purposes.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2013, other loans totaled $5.7 million as compared to $5.2 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012. At December&nbsp;31, 2011, other loans totaled $4.4 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Credit Quality and Allowance for Loan Losses</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A consequence of lending activities is the potential for loss.&#160; The amount of such losses will vary from time to time depending upon the risk characteristics of the loan portfolio as affected by economic conditions, rising interest rates and the financial experience of the borrowers.&#160; The allowance for loan losses, which provides for the risk of losses inherent in the credit extension process, is increased by the provision for loan losses charged to expense and decreased by the amount of charge-offs net of recoveries.&#160; There is no precise method of estimating specific losses or amounts that ultimately may be charged off on particular segments of the loan portfolio.&#160; Similarly, the adequacy of the allowance for loan losses and the level of the related provision for loan losses are determined in management&#146;s judgment based on consideration of:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Economic conditions</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Borrowers&#146; financial condition</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loan impairment</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Evaluation of industry trends</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Historic losses, migrations and delinquency trends</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Industry and other concentrations</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans which are contractually current as to payment terms but demonstrate a higher degree of risk as identified by management</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Continuing evaluation of the performing loan portfolio</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Periodic review and evaluation of problem loans</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Off balance sheet risks</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Assessments by regulators and other third parties</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">33<a name="PB_33_171703_7608"></a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to the internal assessment of the loan portfolio, the Company also retains a consultant who performs credit reviews on a regular basis and then provides an assessment of the adequacy of the allowance for loan losses. All such reviews have confirmed the adequacy of the allowance for loan losses.&#160; The federal banking regulators also conduct examinations of the loan portfolio periodically.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The increase in the allowance for loan losses of $2.0 million from December&nbsp;31, 2012 to $21.9 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013 is primarily attributable to the growth of the loan portfolio. The provision for loan losses for the twelve months ending December&nbsp;31, 2013 and December&nbsp;31, 2012 was $6.1 million and $4.0 million, respectively. The increase in provision for credit losses for the year ending December&nbsp;31, 2013 compared to the same period one year ago was primarily related to the strong growth of the loan portfolio and the charge-off of one asset-based commercial line of credit in the second quarter of 2013.</font></p>

<p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2.78</font></p>    </td>
<td width="1%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 2.25pt 0in;width:1.0%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">%</font></p>    </td>   </tr>  </table>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Beginning in the second quarter of 2008, deterioration in economic conditions within the Company&#146;s market area and, as applicable, the State of California and/or national macroeconomic conditions resulted in increased stress to the loan portfolio, specifically construction and land development loans outside of the Company&#146;s primary market of Santa Clara County and contiguous portions of San Mateo and Alameda counties.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In response to the deteriorating market conditions, the Company undertook steps to aggressively reduce the exposure to construction and land development loans with particular emphasis on reducing loans outside of its primary market area.&#160; Management curtailed new loan origination, thoroughly reviewed collateral values of projects approaching maturity and conservatively evaluated the market prospects of collateral for indications of impairments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2013, the Company&#146;s land development portfolio was $13.6 million with just $452,000 remaining exposure outside of the primary market area.&#160; Further, approximately 16% of the loans in this category are underwritten to amortizing term structures supported by cash flow from liquidity of the borrowers.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Construction loans at December&nbsp;31, 2013 were $51.5 million with $944,000 remaining on projects outside of the primary market area.&#160; In addition, at that date $24.7 million, or 48%, were loans to finance commercial projects.&#160; There were no construction loans to finance residential projects of five or more units.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The aggressive management of credits in this category resulted in elevated levels of nonperforming assets as loans are placed on nonaccrual through the marketing phase of the underlying project.&#160; In addition, loans placed on nonaccrual have been reduced to the level of indicated impairments.&#160; This resulted in an elevated level of charge-offs.&#160; Management believes that this practice results in a recorded level of nonperforming assets that generally has been reduced to a net liquidation value, and as these assets are liquidated do not expect to incur additional significant losses.&#160; Nonperforming loans at December&nbsp;31, 2013, on average, have been reduced by approximately 30% of the remaining contractual balance, which was taken as a charge-off against the allowance for loan losses.&#160; Additionally, non-performing loans at December&nbsp;31, 2013, on average, have been reduced by approximately 9% for payment received in non-accrual interest.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Due to positive trends in overall loan classifications during 2012 and 2013, reflecting the improving condition of the loan portfolio combined with new loan production, the Company has been able to lower the level of reserves to 2.04% of total loans at December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; The coverage ratio, the ratio of allowance for loan losses to nonperforming loans was 145.18% at December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; Management believes that the coverage ratio reflects the conservative charge-off practice and that the allowance is adequate for losses not specifically identified in impairment analyses.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2013 nonperforming assets of $15.1 million, or 0.94% of total assets reflects an increase compared to $10.1 million, or 0.75% of total assets on December&nbsp;31, 2012. The increase in nonperforming assets from December&nbsp;31, 2012 was primarily due to the addition of $18.8 million in non-performing loans, partially offset by $8.3 million in charge-offs and $5.6 million in collections. The addition was primarily comprised of four factoring credits totaling $8.3 million, two commercial and one real estate credit, of $5.2 million and $2.5 million, respectively. The following summarizes nonperforming assets and loans restructured and in compliance with modified terms at December&nbsp;31, 2013, 2012, 2011, 2010, and 2009. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The nonperforming assets at December&nbsp;31, 2013 consisted of sixteen loans on nonaccrual or 90 days or more past due and still accruing totaling $15.1 million, and other real estate owned valued at $31,000. Nonperforming loans at December&nbsp;31, 2013 were comprised of loans with legal contractual balances totaling approximately $24.5 million reduced by $2.1 million received in nonaccrual interest and impairment charges of $7.2 million which have been charged against the allowance for loan losses. As a result, there no longer was an indicated potential loss exposure pertaining to nonperforming loans and no impairment reserves were required to be included in the allowance for loan losses.&#160; There were sixteen non-accrual loans totaling $10.0 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012 and seventeen non-accrual loans totaling $11.8 million at December&nbsp;31, 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The accrual of interest on loans is discontinued and any accrued and unpaid interest is reversed when, in the opinion of Management, there is significant doubt as to the collectability of interest or principal or when the payment of principal or interest is ninety days past due, unless the amount is well-secured and in the process of collection.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Included in nonperforming loans at December&nbsp;31, 2013 are loans totaling $7.4 million that have been modified in trouble debt restructurings, where concessions have been granted to borrowers experiencing financial difficulties.&#160; These concessions could include a reduction in the interest rate on a loan, payment extensions, forgiveness of principal, or other actions intended to maximize collection.&#160; In order for these loans to return to accrual status, the borrower must demonstrate a sustained period of timely payments.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2013, previously modified loans totaling $5.6 million were considered performing due to a sustained period of timely payments and therefore were accounted for on an accrual basis.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management undertakes significant processes in order to identify potential problem loans in a timely manner.&#160; In addition to regular interaction with the Company&#146;s borrowers, the relationship managers review the credit ratings for each loan on a monthly basis and identify any potential downgrades.&#160; For commercial and factoring/asset-based loans, the Company receives quarterly financial statements and other pertinent reporting, such as borrowing bases for asset-based facilities, so as to identify any deteriorating financial trends.&#160; Covenant compliance for these loans is also monitored on a quarterly basis.&#160; For real estate construction and land loans, the development, construction and lease up or sell out status of each project is monitored on a monthly basis.&#160; For SBA loans and loans secured by standing commercial or residential property, the Company receives updated rent rolls, operating statements, and/or tax returns on an annual basis.&#160; In addition, home equity loans are reviewed annually for deterioration in either the underlying property value or the borrower&#146;s payment history.&#160; Management also engages a third party loan review firm that reviews the loan portfolio periodically to further identify potential problem loans.&#160; The loan review includes assessment of underwriting, quality of legal documents, management of the loan relationship, and adherence to the credit policy along with acceptable risk mitigation and rationale for exceptions to the policy.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">37<a name="PB_37_175208_2897"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>
</div>
<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='37',FILE='C:\JMS\106756\14-2726-1\task6613146\2726-1-bs.htm',USER='106756',CD='Mar 11 00:17 2014' -->

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As part of the loan approval process, management identifies the nature and type of underlying collateral supporting individual loans.&#160; Prior to or at the time of initial advances, any required lien positions are verified using UCC lien searches for personal property collateral, or title insurance for real property collateral.&#160; The Company engages a third party loan review firm to conduct an annual review of its loan documentation and the related policies and procedures regarding the loan documentation process.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company primarily relies on fair market appraisals to determine the value of underlying real estate collateral.&#160; Appraisals are required for real property secured loans of $250,000 or more, including increases to existing loans of $250,000 or more.&#160; In the event there is evidence of deterioration in values, an evaluation of the collateral value and/or a full new appraisal is required for an extension of the loan maturity.&#160; Potential problem loans are typically reappraised every 12 months depending size, nature, current economic conditions and the borrower&#146;s current financial performance and repayment history. The appraisals are performed by Board approved appraisers that have appropriate licensing and experience.&#160; Generally, when a prospective loan amount exceeds $3.0 million, the completed appraisal is further reviewed by a qualified third party review appraiser.&#160; To determine the value of underlying collateral for formula lines of credit that are predicated on a borrowing base of eligible assets, the Company typically requires a pre loan funding field audit of the borrower&#146;s financial records to verify the accounts receivable, their eligibility for inclusion in the borrowing base, performance of the collateral and any asset concentrations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On a monthly basis, relationship managers assess the collateral position of individual loans and identify any potential collateral shortfalls which, if left uncorrected, could result in deterioration of the repayment prospects for the loan at some future date.&#160; Any potential collateral shortfalls are incorporated into a written corrective action plan.&#160; The status of the corrective action plans are reviewed by executive management.&#160; Review of ability to acquire additional collateral and the related timeframes are addressed on an individual loan basis.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At the time a loan is classified as substandard (which includes any loan on non-accrual), the Company performs an impairment analysis of the collateral based on appraisals, field audits, other market value indicators, and Management&#146;s judgment.&#160; Any shortfall between the collateral&#146;s realization value and the loan balance is charged-off at that time when management believes the uncollectibility of the loan is confirmed.&#160; Impairment analyses are updated on a monthly basis.&#160; Additionally, as underlying collateral is reappraised the value of the collateral is reassessed and any additional charge-off is taken at that time.&#160; A similar practice is followed for downward adjustments to the Company&#146;s OREO carrying value.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management is of the opinion that the allowance for loan losses is maintained at a level adequate for known and unidentified losses inherent in the portfolio.&#160; However, although the Company is seeing a lower rate of inflow into problem assets generally, as well as a consistent reduction of carrying values through continued payments by borrowers on loans that have been placed on non-accrual, should circumstances change and management determines that the collectibility of any of these credits becomes unlikely, there could be an adverse effect on the level of the allowance for loan losses and the Company&#146;s future profitability.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Funding</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deposits represent the Bank&#146;s principal source of funds.&#160; Most of the Bank&#146;s deposits are obtained from professionals, small- to medium sized businesses and individuals within the Bank&#146;s market area.&#160; The Bank&#146;s deposit base consists of non-interest and interest-bearing demand deposits, money market and savings accounts and certificates of deposit.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table summarizes the composition of deposits as of December&nbsp;31, 2013, 2012 and 2011.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deposits increased $243.5 million or 20.9% from $1.2 billion at December&nbsp;31, 2012 to $1.4 billion at December&nbsp;31, 2013. The increase in deposits was predominately in core deposit production which was primarily used to fund new loans and increase the investment portfolio.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Leverage</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Total gross loan balances at December&nbsp;31, 2013 were $1.1 billion.&#160; The resulting loan to deposit ratio was 76.64%. Other earning assets at December&nbsp;31, 2013 were primarily comprised of investment securities, federal funds sold and interest-bearing deposits of $470.1 million.&#160; To date, the Company has deployed other earning assets primarily in federal funds sold to address the potential volatility of deposit balances and to accommodate projected loan funding, and in short term fixed rate investments to mitigate interest rate risk associated with the Company&#146;s asset-sensitive balance sheet.&#160;&#160; When deploying other earning assets, the Company implements strategic decisions that may have a beneficial or adverse impact on net interest income and on the net interest margin to manage the business through a variety of economic cycles.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Capital Resources</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company and the Bank are subject to the capital guidelines and regulations governing capital adequacy for bank holding companies and national banks.&#160; Additional capital requirements may be imposed on banks based on market risk.&#160; For discussion of capital requirements applicable to the Bank and the Company, see &#147;Capital Adequacy Requirements&#148; and &#147;Prompt Corrective Action&#148; above.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s capital resources consist of shareholders&#146; equity, trust preferred securities and (for regulatory purposes) the allowance for loan losses (subject to limitations).&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2013, the Company&#146;s capital resources increased $17.3 million to $192.8 million from $175.5 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; Tier 1 capital increased $14.4 million to $175.4 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; The Company&#146;s Tier 1 capital at December&nbsp;31, 2013 was comprised of $106.5 million of capital stock and surplus, $51.9 million in retained earnings and trust preferred securities up to the allowable limit of $17.0 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s Tier 1 capital at December&nbsp;31, 2012 was $161.1 million, which was comprised of $106.8 million of capital stock and surplus, $37.2 million in retained earnings and trust preferred securities up to the allowable limit of $17.0 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is subject to capital adequacy guidelines issued by the Board of Governors and the OCC. The Company is required to maintain total capital equal to at least 8.0% of assets and commitments to extend credit, weighted by risk, of which at least 4.0% must consist primarily of common equity including retained earnings (Tier 1 capital) and the remainder may consist of subordinated debt, cumulative preferred stock or a limited amount of allowance for loan losses.&#160; Certain assets and commitments to extend credit present less risk than others and will be assigned to lower risk-weighted categories requiring less capital allocation than the 8.0% total ratio.&#160; For example, cash and government securities are assigned to a 0.0% risk-weighted category, most home mortgage loans are assigned to a 50.0% risk-weighted category requiring a 4.0% capital allocation and commercial loans are assigned to a 100.0% risk-weighted category requiring an 8.0% capital allocation.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2013, the Company&#146;s and the Bank&#146;s total risk-based capital ratios were 13.96% and 12.25%, respectively (15.23% for the Company and 13.08% for the Bank at December&nbsp;31, 2012).</font></p>

<p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">5.00</font></p>    </td>
<td width="2%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:2.5%;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>

<p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">5.00</font></p>    </td>
<td width="1%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.0%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">%</font></p>    </td>   </tr>  </table>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The federal banking agencies, including the OCC, have adopted regulations implementing a system of prompt corrective action under FDICIA.&#160; The regulations establish five capital categories with the following characteristics:&#160; (1)&nbsp;&#147;Well capitalized,&#148; consisting of institutions with a total risk-based capital ratio of 10.0% or greater, a Tier&nbsp;1 risk-based capital ratio of 6.0% or greater and a leverage ratio of 5.0% or greater and which are not operating under an order, written agreement, capital directive or prompt corrective action directive; (2)&nbsp;&#147;Adequately capitalized,&#148; consisting of institutions with a total risk-based capital ratio of 8.0% or greater, a Tier&nbsp;1 risk-based capital of 4.0% or greater and a leverage ratio of 4.0% or greater and which do not meet the definition of a &#147;well capitalized&#148; institution; (3)&nbsp;&#147;Undercapitalized,&#148; consisting of institutions with a total risk-based capital ratio of less than 8.0%, a Tier&nbsp;1 risk-based capital ratio of less than 4.0%, or a leverage ratio of less than 4.0%; (4)&nbsp;&#147;Significantly undercapitalized,&#148; consisting of institutions with a total risk-based capital ratio of less than 6.0%, a Tier&nbsp;1 risk-based capital ratio of less than 3.0%, or a leverage ratio of less than 3.0%; and (5)&nbsp;&#147;Critically undercapitalized,&#148; consisting of institutions with a ratio of tangible equity to total assets that is equal to or less than 2.0%.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial institutions classified as undercapitalized or below are subject to various limitations including, among other matters, certain supervisory actions by bank regulatory authorities and restrictions related to (i)&nbsp;growth of assets, (ii) payment of interest on subordinated indebtedness, (iii)&nbsp;payment of dividends or other capital distributions, and (iv)&nbsp;payment of management fees to a parent holding company.&#160; The FDICIA requires the bank regulatory authorities to initiate corrective action regarding financial institutions that fail to meet minimum capital requirements.&#160; Such action may result in orders to, among other matters, augment capital and reduce total assets.&#160; Critically undercapitalized financial institutions may also be subject to appointment of a receiver or implementation of a capitalization plan.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In response to increasing risk perceived in the economic environment, during the fourth quarter of 2008 the Company raised $53.9 million of additional capital.&#160; Additionally, to support tangible common equity as a component of Tier 1 capital and to ensure resources for the eventual TARP repayment, the Company completed the sale of $30.0 million in common stock to a group of institutional investors in a private placement transaction during the fourth quarter of 2010.&#160; </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">40<a name="PB_40_180107_141"></a></font></p>

<div>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following is a summary of these issuances:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;17, 2008, The Company sold $30.0 million of its Series&nbsp;B and B-1 Convertible Preferred Stock to the Carpenter Community BancFunds (the &#147;Carpenter Funds&#148;) in a private placement or approximately 31.3% of the Company&#146;s common stock on an as-converted basis.&#160; In connection with this sale, the Company granted certain participation and investor rights to the Carpenter Funds.&#160; On March&nbsp;31, 2010, the Company and the Carpenter Funds agreed to the early conversion of the preferred stock and, a result of the conversion, the Company issued a total of 3,710,289 shares of its common stock and convertible promissory notes in the aggregate principal amount of $789,860 (the &#147;Notes&#148;). On June&nbsp;17, 2010, the Notes converted into 93,364 shares of common stock.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;23, 2008, the Company sold 23,864 shares of its Series&nbsp;C Preferred Stock and a warrant to purchase up to 396,412 shares of common stock to the U.S. Department of the Treasury on the TARP Capital Purchase Program for proceeds of $23.9 million.&#160; On March&nbsp;16, 2011, the Company fully redeemed its Series&nbsp;C Preferred Stock for $23.9 million. On April&nbsp;20, 2011, the Company repurchased the warrant for $1.4 million, which was recorded as a reduction to shareholders&#146; equity.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;23, 2010, the Company sold investors 3,508,771 shares of its common stock in a private placement for an aggregate purchase price of $30.0 million.&#160; The investors included the Carpenter Funds, which purchased 1,103,275 common shares.&#160; Upon the completion of the private placement, the Carpenter Funds held a total of 4,906,928 shares of the Company&#146;s common stock or approximately 33.9% of the Company&#146;s outstanding shares of common stock.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 7a. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk</font></u></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Liquidity/Interest Rate Sensitivity</font></u></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company strives to manage its liquidity to provide adequate funds at an acceptable cost to support the borrowing requirements and deposit flows of its customers. Liquidity requirements are evaluated by taking into consideration factors such as deposit concentrations, seasonality and maturities, loan and lease demand, capital expenditures and prevailing and anticipated economic conditions.&#160; The Company&#146;s business is generated primarily through customer referrals and employee business development efforts.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is primarily a business and professional bank and, as such, its deposit base is more susceptible to economic fluctuations.&#160; The Company strives to maintain a balanced position of liquid assets to volatile and cyclical deposits. At December&nbsp;31, 2013, liquid assets as a percentage of deposits were 34.2% as compared to 33.0% in 2012.&#160; In addition to cash and due from banks, liquid assets include interest-bearing deposits with other banks, federal funds sold, and unpledged securities available for sale.&#160; The Company has $47.0 million in Federal funds lines of credit available with correspondent banks to meet liquidity needs.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2013, there were no balances outstanding on these lines. Additionally, as of December&nbsp;31, 2013, the Company had a total borrowing capacity with the Federal Home Loan Bank of San Francisco of approximately $368.0 million for which the Company had collateral in place to borrow $77.0 million.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2013, $10.0 million of this borrowing capacity was pledged to secure a letter of credit.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s balance sheet position is asset-sensitive (based upon the significant amount of variable rate loans and the repricing characteristics of its deposit accounts).&#160;&#160; This balance sheet position generally provides a hedge against rising interest rates, but has a detrimental effect during times of interest rate decreases.&#160; Net interest income is generally negatively impacted in the short term by a decline in interest rates.&#160; Conversely, an increase in interest rates should have a short-term positive impact on net interest income.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management regularly reviews general economic and financial conditions, both external and internal, and determines whether the positions taken with respect to liquidity and interest rate sensitivity continue to be appropriate.&#160; The Bank utilizes a monthly &#147;Gap&#148; report as well as a quarterly simulation model to identify interest rate sensitivity over the short- and long-term.&#160; Management considers the results of these analyses when implementing its interest rate risk management activities, including the utilization of certain interest rate hedges.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<td width="2%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:2.0%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>
<td width="10%" colspan="2" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:10.0%;">
<p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>
<td width="1%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.0%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>   </tr>  </table>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Based on the contractual terms of its assets and liabilities, the Bank&#146;s balance sheet at December&nbsp;31, 2013 was asset sensitive in terms of its short-term exposure to interest rates.&#160; That is, at December&nbsp;31, 2013 the volume of assets that might reprice within the next year exceeded the volume of liabilities that might reprice.&#160; This position provides a hedge against rising interest rates, but has a detrimental effect during times of rate decreases.&#160; Net interest income is negatively impacted by a decline in interest rates and positively impacted by an increase in interest rates.&#160; To partially mitigate the adverse impact of declining rates, the majority of variable rate loans made by the Bank have been written with a minimum &#147;floor&#148; rate.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">42<a name="PB_42_180649_8146"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table shows maturities of the loan portfolio at December&nbsp;31, 2013 and 2012.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2013, approximately 77.5% of the loan portfolio is priced with floating interest rates which limit the exposure to interest rate risk on long-term loans.</font></p>
